verification.root_cause: ⛔ MEASURED THREE WAYS, AND MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG. (1) TIMING: the nine most recent completed runs on main are all `cancelled`, each 1-3 s after the NEXT run on main is created — 8c14cc5 cancelled 20:24:23 as 3937db8 was created 20:24:22, and so on through 12a5f34. (2) THE DISCRIMINATOR: run 33207278897 on 86098c2 was `pending`, NOT running, when cancelled — `cancel-in-progress` only ever cancels a RUNNING run, and it already evaluated to false on main. So the flag was never the mechanism. (3) PLATFORM SEMANTICS READ LIVE, NOT REMEMBERED: a concurrency group holds at most one running and one pending run; a third arrival evicts the pending one whatever the flag says. ⭐ MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS — that the expression evaluates to a truthy string 'false' — is NOT what the evidence shows, and observation (2) is what killed it.
verification.chain_closed: gates_verdict.py's own line 96 reads '`cancelled` and `skipped` are NOT verdicts. A cancelled run says the trunk was never tested', and it returns `_no_verdict` when no graded run is in the window. So the eviction is the concrete mechanism behind health.py's `gates_green` reading NO-GATE-VERDICT for 47.2 h — a row every cycle reads before it starts.
verification.mutation_testing: 4/4 caught, single-site, in a worktree: M9 revert to the shared ref group, M10 uniquify every ref not just main, M11 drop ref entirely, M12 branches stop collapsing. Log: drv-mutation3.log.
verification.honest_limit: ⛔ THE GUARD READS THE WORKFLOW FILE, NOT GITHUB. It can show the configuration no longer forces runs to evict one another; it CANNOT show that runs are now completing. That is gates_verdict.py's half, and it stays UNMEASURED until a run on main actually finishes — which this cycle's own push is the first chance to observe.

what_i_got_wrong: Reached for the familiar explanation first — that an expression-valued `cancel-in-progress` coerces to a truthy string. It is a real Actions gotcha and it was not this. The pending-run cancellation is what discriminated, and I only looked for it because CLAUDE.md §4 requires the observation that separates competing hypotheses rather than the one that fits the favourite.
Misread a gate as stalled when it had started one minute earlier, and said so before checking the log's mtime. Checking took one command and should have come first.
